record.original_question: In generic inhomogeneous cosmological spacetimes approaching a spacelike singularity, can one prove the BKL locality conjecture, namely that the asymptotic dynamics become local along timelines except for any exceptional nonlocal structures that must be handled separately?

evidence.quote: Problem P14: Prove the BKL locality conjecture in the general inhomoge￰neous context.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a four-dimensional Lorentzian spacetime $(M,g)$ satisfying the vacuum Einstein equations (or, more generally, the Einstein equations coupled to standard matter such as a perfect fluid or scalar field) and admitting a spacelike singularity that is approached as a synchronous time coordinate $t$ tends to $0^+$. Pick a generic inhomogeneous initial data set, i.e. one not constrained by additional symmetries.

The Belinski–Khalatnikov–Lifshitz (BKL) locality conjecture asserts that, as $t\to 0^+$, the dynamics of the gravitational field becomes asymptotically local along timelines: namely, after suitable rescaling, the spatial-derivative terms in the Einstein evolution equations become negligible compared to the time-derivative terms, so that at almost every spatial point the field evolves according to a system of ordinary differential equations in $t$ (the truncated, spatially homogeneous "Mixmaster" or Kasner-type dynamics) — possibly excluding a measure-zero set of exceptional spatial points where genuinely nonlocal structures (such as spikes) form and must be analysed separately.

Problem. Provide a rigorous mathematical proof (or disproof) of the BKL locality conjecture for generic inhomogeneous solutions of the vacuum Einstein equations approaching a spacelike singularity, including a precise characterization and treatment of the exceptional nonlocal structures.
artifact.status_search_result: The BKL locality conjecture remains unproven in the general inhomogeneous setting. Rigorous proofs exist only in special symmetric cases (e.g., Gowdy spacetimes and other symmetry-reduced models), and numerical simulations of generic inhomogeneous collapse continue to provide strong supporting evidence, but no general mathematical proof has appeared.

status_evidence.title: BKL singularity - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The BKL conjecture conjectures that one should expect a generic singularity in spatially inhomogeneous cosmologies to be locally of the Mixmaster type.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is stated as a still-open expectation about generic inhomogeneous cosmological singularities.

status_evidence.title: Numerical Approaches to Spacetime Singularities
status_evidence.snippet: In the general case, the strongest evidence to date comes from numerical evolutions... numerical simulations of collapsing, spatially inhomogeneous cosmological spacetimes have provided strong support for the BKL picture.
status_evidence.claim: In the general inhomogeneous case the support for BKL locality is numerical, not a rigorous proof.

status_evidence.title: The Cosmological Singularity (Cambridge)
status_evidence.snippet: Up-to-date mathematical derivation of the theory underlying the Belinski–Khalatnikov–Lifshitz (BKL) conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Mathematical frameworks supporting BKL continue to be developed but a full proof in the inhomogeneous case is not established.
